B.Tech · Electronics and Computer Engineering

Build the whole smart device.

Design a circuit board, write its firmware and run AI on the device. Take a working prototype through a pilot batch and a field trial.

Book a campus visit

How a smart device works

A smartwatch, an EV charger and a heart monitor each depend on circuits and software working together. This course follows the work across that boundary, from a sensor reading to a device someone can use.

From calibrated instrument to field trial

Semester 1 A smart measuring instrument

Design and calibrate your own instrument.

Semester 2 A connected device with a custom circuit board

Build a working device on a circuit board you designed.

Semester 3 An embedded board

Make your own board process a real-world signal.

Semester 4 Real-time motor control

Build a controller that balances, steers or drives a motor.

Semester 5 On-device AI on Linux

Build a Linux-based product that runs a model on the device itself.

Semester 6 A 10-unit pilot batch

Build a secure product and make a pilot batch of 10 units.

Semester 7 A smart device in field trials

Take a complete smart device from a user's problem to a field trial.

Semester 8 16–20 weeks of engineering work

Put your skills to work in a company or the Product Studio.

Circuits, firmware and edge AI

Hardware

Circuit and PCB design, ARM and RISC-V microcontrollers, FPGA, and design for manufacturing.

Software

C, C++ and Python, real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, device drivers and device security.

Embedded intelligence

Signal processing, control, machine learning and edge AI.

Where it leads

Explore work in embedded systems and firmware, edge AI, embedded Linux, IoT products, and automotive and EV electronics. The skills also support building a hardware startup.

For those who want the detail

The sequence starts with measurement and circuit design, then introduces embedded computing and real-time control. Later builds bring together on-device machine learning, device security, pilot manufacturing and a field trial. Individual practical assessments document what each student can do independently.

See how projects and skill tests work

Common questions

What does Electronics and Computer Engineering cover?

It combines electronics and computer engineering in one degree. You design the hardware, write the software and learn how the two work together.

Can I take a software job?

Yes. The curriculum includes programming, data structures, operating systems and software engineering.
